source.title: LUCID-SAE: Learning Unified Vision-Language Sparse Codes for Interpretable Concept Discovery
source.authors: Di-Fei Gu; Yun-He Gao; Gerasimos Chatzoudis; Zi-Han Dong; Guo-Ning Zhang; Bang-Wei Guo; Yang Zhou; Mu Zhou; Dimitris N. Metaxas

record.file_problem: Text is a full paper with appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies sparse-autoencoder feature discovery to a vision-language model and reports learned concept features and their interpretations. This extends SAE feature-recovery evidence to a multimodal setting; it does not reproduce toy-model superposition experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses superposition and cites Toy Models of Superposition, but does not test toy networks, feature sparsity-dependent transitions, importance-dependent geometry, or superposition directions. Its own results concern LUCID's learned SAE codes and their semantic interpretations. Reconstruction, grounding, and clustering-comparison scores are not treated as direct tests of toy-model geometry or of whether features are complete, stable canonical units.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper. It assumes SAEs disentangle superposed features, then reports only its own LUCID SAE's results: reconstruction R², grounding, clustering degeneracy and qualitative neuron interpretations on SigLIP ViT-B/16. There is no comparison against raw neurons or any baseline that would bear on whether the model holds features in superposition. The subject is also a vision-language encoder, not an LLM.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that the shared-private decomposition improves reconstruction and cross-modal predictability, and that OT/GCMT alignment improves patch-level grounding. They say structured shared-code objectives reduce clustering degeneracy, and that the automated pipeline finds coherent concepts that generalize to ImageNet. They make no claim about superposition itself.
record.recipe_differences: This is a unified Top-k SAE with shared and modality-private codes plus optimal-transport alignment, trained on SigLIP ViT-B/16 activations. It does not use or reproduce the toy-network experiments or measurements from Toy Models of Superposition.
record.method_sensitivity: The study compares shared-only capacity (r=1.0) with shared-plus-private capacity (r=0.25), and compares OT-only, Share-k, GSL, and GCMT configurations for grounding and clustering diagnostics. These configuration results do not test the claim's superposition geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: A Top-k SAE with shared and private codes on SigLIP ViT-B/16 (vision-language) yields shared units that the authors interpret as coherent concepts. This is shown qualitatively, for neurons filtered by cluster purity ≥0.55.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionaries trained on vision-language encoder activations recover human-interpretable, cross-modally aligned concepts.

record.problems: The semantic-neuron evidence is qualitative and reported for 12 randomly selected neurons, with an interpretation pipeline that filters for minimum concept hits and dominant-cluster purity of at least 0.55. The text reports no uncertainty estimates for the listed feature interpretations. Results concern one vision-language backbone and do not validate learned SAE features as complete or canonical units.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 2-4 report reconstruction, grounding, and clustering-diagnostic comparisons among LUCID configurations. They are not separate tests of the listed superposition claims: the reconstruction scores do not establish feature geometry, and the grounding/configuration comparisons do not measure feature competition, stability, completeness, or one-dimensionality. No direct toy-model superposition result is reported.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
No test of the capacity account of polysemanticity.
No test of other causes of polysemanticity.
No comparison of SAE features with raw neurons. No LLM is studied, and there is no quantitative interpretability rate for features.
No tests of completeness, stability or canonicity.
Dimensionality of features is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T3 to uses_without_test/T4. The neuron results are the study's own method's qualitative outputs, after a purity filter, with no baseline. The rows are kept but unlinked. The paper is inconsistent on training data: Section 4.1 says COCO plus CC3M, while Appendix A.1 says COCO train only. The neurons are called 'randomly selected' but are also filtered for purity.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise from limited capacity, whether important features get dedicated dimensions, and whether other features share dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity occurs without capacity pressure.

The study tests SAE feature discovery on SigLIP ViT-B/16, a vision-language model, not language-only LLMs; it does not establish that the discovered codes are the model's underlying canonical features.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable across settings, or canonical units of the model's representation.
Whether the underlying superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: SigLIP ViT-B/16
rows.stage_stated: LUCID SAE trained on MS COCO 2017 train split for 200 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Clustered top-activating text concepts associated with shared SAE neurons.
rows.measure: Dominant semantic cluster of associated concepts
rows.value: Kitchen and indoor concepts, including cutting, kitchen sink, cabinet, countertop, stove, and oven.
rows.note: The table reports this neuron as one of 12 randomly selected shared neurons.
rows.check: Qualitative interpretation of the study's own SAE neuron, kept after a purity ≥0.55 filter, so it is a selection result. No baseline. The term list includes off-theme items (wallet, cookie, shoe).

rows.subject: SigLIP ViT-B/16
rows.stage_stated: LUCID SAE trained on MS COCO 2017 train split for 200 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated shared-code concept activations on COCO images using spatial activation maps.

conditions.value: Examples from scenes, objects, animals, colors, actions, and quantities

rows.measure: Semantic relevance and spatial localization of discovered concepts
rows.value: The paper reports localized activations for concepts including bathroom, bedroom, glass, bicycle, cat, elephant, brown, orange, skiing, walking, many, and group.
rows.note: Examples are shown for randomly selected semantic categories; the paper describes the activation maps as spatially precise.
rows.check: Cherry-presentable heatmap examples from the study's own method. No quantitative rate and no baseline.

rows.subject: SigLIP ViT-B/16
rows.stage_stated: LUCID SAE trained on MS COCO 2017 train split for 200 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Applied the learned dictionary to ImageNet images.

conditions.value: Camouflage, flying, grass, holding, top, and water

rows.measure: Semantic relevance and spatial localization of discovered concepts
rows.value: The paper reports semantically meaningful activation patterns that localize to natural patterns, birds with sky context, ground vegetation, and other relevant image evidence.
rows.note: This is an evaluation of the same learned dictionary outside its training distribution.
rows.check: Qualitative out-of-distribution heatmap examples from the study's own method. No quantitative measure.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Selected shared LUCID SAE neurons and concept examples on COCO; selected concepts on ImageNet
reader_labels.reason: The reported neuron clusters and localized concept activations provide evidence that an SAE can yield interpretable sparse codes from SigLIP ViT-B/16 representations (r1-r14).
